interview.q: Why do I get "Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0" from my API call?
interview.a: The response starts with "<", so it is HTML (a 404/500 page, login redirect or index.html fallback), not JSON. Check the URL, status and Content-Type in the Network tab.

interview.q: How should you handle 204 No Content?
interview.a: Do not call res.json(); it has an empty body and throws "Unexpected end of JSON input". Return null/undefined when status is 204 or the text is empty.

interview.q: How do you avoid losing precision for large ids?
interview.a: JSON numbers above 2^53 lose precision in JavaScript. Send them as strings (or use BigInt with a custom reviver).

pitfalls: if (localStorage) throws in sandboxed iframes and blocked-cookie modes - the check itself needs try/catch.
Using localStorage for tokens exposes them to XSS.
topics.title: localStorage Errors: QuotaExceededError and SecurityError
topics.summary: Storage can throw: it may be full, disabled, blocked in private mode or in sandboxed iframes. Wrap it defensively.
topics.description:
`localStorage` and `sessionStorage` look simple, but they can **throw** in several situations:

| Error | When | Message (Chrome) |
|---|---|---|
| `QuotaExceededError` (DOMException) | ~5 MB per origin exceeded; Safari private mode (old) set quota to 0 | `Failed to execute 'setItem' on 'Storage': Setting the value of 'key' exceeded the quota.` |
| `SecurityError` | storage blocked: "Block third-party cookies", cookies disabled, sandboxed iframe without `allow-same-origin`, `file://` in some browsers, opaque origin | `Failed to read the 'localStorage' property from 'Window': Access is denied for this document.` |
| `ReferenceError` / `undefined` | Node.js, Web Worker, SSR (no `localStorage` there) | `localStorage is not defined` |
| `SyntaxError` | `JSON.parse` of corrupted value | `Unexpected token...` |
| `TypeError` | circular object in `JSON.stringify` | `Converting circular structure to JSON` |

Notice that merely **reading** the `window.localStorage` property can throw `SecurityError` - so a check like `if (window.localStorage)` must also be inside `try/catch`.

### Defensive pattern
1. Feature-test once inside `try/catch` by writing and removing a test key.
2. Wrap `get`/`set` in helpers that parse JSON safely and return defaults.
3. On `QuotaExceededError` (check `e.name === "QuotaExceededError"` or the legacy `e.code === 22`; Firefox old name `NS_ERROR_DOM_QUOTA_REACHED` / code 1014): remove old entries (cache eviction/LRU), or fall back to memory.
4. Keep an **in-memory fallback** (a `Map`) so the app still works.
5. Version your stored data (`{v: 2, data}`) and ignore invalid old formats.

### Don'ts
- Don't store large data (images, big JSON) in localStorage; use **IndexedDB** (hundreds of MB, async) or the Cache API.
- Don't store secrets or tokens that XSS could steal (prefer `HttpOnly` cookies).
- Remember storage is **synchronous** and blocks the main thread; large reads are slow.
- Values are always strings: store `"undefined"` by mistake (`setItem(k, undefined)`) and `JSON.parse` later throws.

### Check usage
`navigator.storage.estimate()` returns `{ usage, quota }` for the origin (IndexedDB, Cache, etc.).
keyPoints: setItem can throw QuotaExceededError; reading window.localStorage can throw SecurityError.
Always wrap storage access in try/catch and provide an in-memory fallback.
Values are strings: stringify/parse safely and never store undefined.
Use IndexedDB for large data; storage is synchronous.
navigator.storage.estimate() shows usage and quota.

interview.q: Why can localStorage throw?
interview.a: The quota (about 5 MB) can be exceeded (QuotaExceededError), and storage can be blocked by privacy settings or sandboxed iframes (SecurityError), even on property access.

interview.q: Where should large client-side data go instead?
interview.a: IndexedDB (async, much larger quotas) or the Cache API. localStorage is small, synchronous and string-only.

interview.q: How do you detect localStorage safely?
interview.a: Inside try/catch, write and remove a test key; any exception means it is unavailable.

topics.title: DOM Errors: null Elements, querySelector and Timing
topics.summary: Why getElementById returns null, how to avoid "Cannot read properties of null", and invalid selector errors.
topics.description:
The DOM is the top source of `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null` in front-end code.

### Why you get null
| Cause | Explanation | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **Script runs before the element exists** | `<script>` in `<head>` runs while the body is not parsed | put script at end of `<body>`, add `defer`, use `type="module"` (deferred), or `DOMContentLoaded` |
| **Wrong selector** | typo, missing `#` or `.`, wrong id/class | check in DevTools Elements, use `document.querySelector("#id")` |
| **Element added later** | rendered by JS/framework after your code ran | query after render; use event delegation or `MutationObserver` |
| **Inside another document** | iframe, Shadow DOM | query the `shadowRoot` / `contentDocument` |
| **Duplicate or changed id** | framework re-created the node | re-query, don't cache stale nodes |
| **Calling `document.getElementById("#id")`** | `getElementById` takes the id **without** `#` | remove `#` |

### DOMException messages
- `Failed to execute 'querySelector' on 'Document': '#1abc' is not a valid selector.` - ids starting with a digit or containing special characters need `CSS.escape("1abc")`.
- `InvalidCharacterError: String contains an invalid character` - `createElement("<div>")` (give only the tag name).
- `HierarchyRequestError`, `NotFoundError` (see DOMException topics).
- `TypeError: Failed to execute 'appendChild' on 'Node': parameter 1 is not of type 'Node'.` - passing a string/null.
- `TypeError: Cannot set properties of null (setting 'textContent')`.

### Defensive code
```js
const el = document.querySelector("#price");
if (!el) return;                // or throw a clear error: new Error("#price not found")
el.textContent = total;
// or
document.querySelector("#price")?.append(total);
```
Prefer `textContent` over `innerHTML` for text (also avoids XSS). Use `element.closest()`, `matches()` and event delegation for dynamic content.

### Remember
`querySelectorAll` returns a (possibly empty) NodeList and never null. `getElementById` and `querySelector` return `null` when nothing matches.
keyPoints: getElementById / querySelector return null when nothing matches; querySelectorAll returns an empty list.
Script ran before the DOM was ready: use defer, module scripts or DOMContentLoaded.
getElementById takes the id without #.
Escape ids/classes with CSS.escape for querySelector.
Guard with if (!el) or optional chaining.

pitfalls: Silencing every ResizeObserver message globally can also hide real layout loops during development.
Reporting every "Failed to fetch" floods dashboards when users lose connectivity.
topics.title: "Script error.", ResizeObserver Loop and Other Benign Errors
topics.summary: Cross-origin "Script error." with no details, the harmless ResizeObserver loop message and other noise your monitoring should filter.
topics.description:
### "Script error."
When an uncaught error comes from a script loaded from **another origin** (a CDN, a third-party widget), browsers hide the details to prevent information leaks. `window.onerror` receives:
`message: "Script error."  source: ""  line: 0  col: 0  error: null`

To get real information:
1. Add `crossorigin="anonymous"` to the `<script>` tag.
2. Make the CDN respond with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` (most CDNs already do).
3. Self-host the script, or use a source map-aware monitoring tool.
Same-origin code does not have this problem.

### ResizeObserver loop messages
`ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.` (older: `ResizeObserver loop limit exceeded`) appears when a ResizeObserver callback changes layout so that another resize is triggered in the same frame. It is a **warning-level error event, not an exception**: nothing breaks, no stack trace, `event.error` is `null`. Fix by changing sizes inside `requestAnimationFrame`, or ignore the message in your error reporter.

### Other noise to filter in monitoring
| Message | Source |
|---|---|
| `Script error.` | cross-origin without CORS |
| `ResizeObserver loop ...` | layout feedback, benign |
| `Non-Error promise rejection captured` | someone rejected with a string/object |
| `Extension context invalidated`, `chrome-extension://` in stack | browser extensions |
| `Load failed` / `Failed to fetch` | user went offline or navigated away mid-request (Safari/Chrome) |
| `AbortError` | intentional cancellation |
| `The operation is insecure` | storage in blocked contexts |
| `Java object is gone`, `window.webkit.messageHandlers` | in-app browsers |

### Error event shapes
- `ErrorEvent` (runtime): `message, filename, lineno, colno, error`.
- Resource errors (image/script load failure) are plain `Event` on the element; they do **not bubble**, so listen with `addEventListener("error", fn, true)` (capture) on `window`.
- `PromiseRejectionEvent` has `reason` and `promise`.

### A good filter
Ignore by message prefix, extension URLs and known third-party hosts, but keep a counter so you notice if they spike.
keyPoints: "Script error." means a cross-origin script threw; add crossorigin="anonymous" and CORS headers.
ResizeObserver loop messages are benign; they have no stack and break nothing.
Resource load errors do not bubble: capture them with addEventListener("error", fn, true).
Filter noise (extensions, aborts, offline) in your error reporter.
Non-Error rejections ("Non-Error promise rejection captured") come from code rejecting with plain values.

Cross-origin scripts and resource errors

interview.q: Why is the error message just "Script error."?
interview.a: The script came from another origin without CORS, so the browser hides details for security. Load it with crossorigin="anonymous" and serve Access-Control-Allow-Origin.

interview.q: Is the ResizeObserver loop error dangerous?
interview.a: No. It is a notification that layout changed again in the same frame. Defer layout changes with requestAnimationFrame or ignore the message.

interview.q: Why do image/script load errors not reach window.onerror?
interview.a: Resource errors fire on the element and do not bubble. Register a capturing error listener on window to see them.

pitfalls: Auto-reloading on chunk errors without a guard can create endless reload loops.
Deleting old hashed assets immediately on deploy breaks users who still have the old HTML open.
topics.title: Module Loading and Service Worker Errors
topics.summary: Failed dynamic imports (ChunkLoadError), MIME-type and specifier errors, and Service Worker registration/update failures.
topics.description:
### Static and dynamic import errors
| Message | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Failed to resolve module specifier "react". Relative references must start with either "/", "./", or "../".` | bare import without bundler / import map | bundle, or add an `importmap` |
| `Failed to load module script: Expected a JavaScript module script but the server responded with a MIME type of "text/html"` | wrong path (404 page) or SPA fallback | fix path; serve `.js` as `text/javascript` |
| `Failed to load module script: The server responded with a non-JavaScript MIME type of ""` | server sends wrong `Content-Type` for `.mjs`/`.js` | configure MIME types |
| `The requested module './x.js' does not provide an export named 'y'` | wrong named import, CommonJS module | check export; use default import |
| `TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: https://.../chunk-ab12.js` (Chrome) / `error loading dynamically imported module` (Firefox) / `Importing a module script failed.` (Safari) | **chunk file missing after a new deploy**, offline, CORS | reload the page; keep old assets for a while; retry |
| `Loading chunk 12 failed.` / `ChunkLoadError` (webpack) | same: stale HTML points to deleted chunks | same |
| `Cannot use import statement outside a module` | classic script | `type="module"` |
| `Cross-Origin Request Blocked` for module scripts | module scripts always use CORS | send CORS headers |
| `file:// import blocked` | modules do not work on `file://` | use a local server |

### Handling dynamic import failures
```js
async function loadWithRetry(loader, retries = 2) {
  for (let i = 0; ; i++) {
    try { return await loader(); }
    catch (e) { if (i >= retries) throw e; await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 300 * 2 ** i)); }
  }
}
const Chart = await loadWithRetry(() => import("./chart.js"));
```
After final failure show "A new version is available - reload" and call `location.reload()` (once!, guard with `sessionStorage` to avoid reload loops).

### Service Worker errors
| Error | Meaning / fix |
|---|---|
| `SecurityError: Failed to register a ServiceWorker... The origin of the provided scriptURL does not match` | script must be same origin |
| `A bad HTTP response code (404) was received when fetching the script.` | wrong path or scope |
| `The script has an unsupported MIME type ('text/html')` | server returns HTML for the SW file |
| `Failed to register ... The path of the provided scope is not under the max scope allowed` | SW file location limits scope; move it to root or send `Service-Worker-Allowed` |
| `InvalidStateError: ... The document is in an invalid state` | registering from a detached document |
| `TypeError: Failed to update a ServiceWorker: An unknown error occurred when fetching the script.` | offline during update check |
| `Failed to execute 'addAll' on 'Cache': Request failed` | one URL in `cache.addAll` failed (404/CORS) so install fails |
| HTTP only | Service workers require HTTPS (localhost is exempt) |

Debug in DevTools → **Application → Service Workers** (Update on reload, Bypass for network, Unregister) and the **Cache Storage** viewer.
keyPoints: Failed dynamic imports after a deploy are usually stale chunk URLs: retry, then ask for a reload.
MIME type text/html for a module means a 404 or SPA fallback is being served.
Bare module specifiers need a bundler or an import map.
cache.addAll fails entirely if any single request fails, which breaks SW installation.
Service workers need HTTPS (except localhost) and a same-origin script under the allowed scope.

}
</script>

interview.q: Why do dynamic imports fail right after deploying a new version?
interview.a: Users with the old HTML request old hashed chunk files that no longer exist on the server. Keep old assets for a while, retry, and prompt a reload.

interview.q: What does a "MIME type of text/html" module error mean?
interview.a: The server returned an HTML page (404 or SPA fallback) for a module URL. Fix the path or server routing.

interview.q: Why can cache.addAll break service worker installation?
interview.a: It is atomic: if any single request fails, the whole promise rejects and the install event fails. Use individual cache.add with allSettled for optional files.

Trusting that a message was delivered: WebSocket has no built-in acknowledgements.
topics.title: WebSocket Errors, Close Codes and Reconnection
topics.summary: Understand the opaque error event, close codes like 1006, InvalidStateError on send, and reconnect with backoff.
topics.description:
The browser `WebSocket` API deliberately gives **very little** error detail.

### Events
```js
const ws = new WebSocket("wss://example.com/socket");
ws.onopen    = () => ...;
ws.onmessage = (e) => ...;
ws.onerror   = (e) => ...;   // plain Event: NO message, NO status code (security)
ws.onclose   = (e) => ...;   // e.code, e.reason, e.wasClean
```
`onerror` is always followed by `onclose`. The real information is the **close code**.

### Close codes
| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `1000` | normal closure |
| `1001` | going away (page navigation, server shutdown) |
| `1006` | **abnormal closure**: no close frame (network drop, server crash, connection refused, handshake failed, proxy timeout) - never sent by code, only reported locally |
| `1008` | policy violation |
| `1009` | message too big |
| `1011` | server internal error |
| `1012/1013` | service restart / try again later |
| `4000-4999` | application-defined (custom: auth failed, kicked...) |

### Errors you can get
| Message | Cause |
|---|---|
| `WebSocket connection to 'wss://...' failed: ` (console) | server down, wrong URL/port, TLS error, proxy not forwarding `Upgrade` |
| `WebSocket opening handshake was canceled` | closed before connecting |
| `Error during WebSocket handshake: Unexpected response code: 401/403/404` | auth cookie/origin check failed or wrong path |
| `SyntaxError: Failed to construct 'WebSocket': The URL 'http://...' is invalid. The scheme must be 'ws' or 'wss'` | wrong scheme |
| `SecurityError: ... An insecure WebSocket connection may not be initiated from a page loaded over HTTPS` | use `wss://` (mixed content) |
| `InvalidStateError: Failed to execute 'send' on 'WebSocket': Still in CONNECTING state.` | `send` before `onopen` |
| `Failed to execute 'send' ...: WebSocket is already in CLOSING or CLOSED state` (warning) | sending after close - messages are dropped |

### Production checklist
1. **Reconnect** automatically with exponential backoff + jitter (cap at ~30 s).
2. **Queue** outgoing messages while disconnected.
3. **Heartbeat** (ping/pong messages) to detect half-open connections.
4. Check `ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN` before `send`.
5. Authenticate via first message or cookie/ticket in the URL (browsers cannot set custom headers).
6. Re-subscribe after reconnect; treat messages as possibly lost.
keyPoints: ws.onerror gives no details; read the code in onclose.
Code 1006 = abnormal closure (no close frame): network/server/handshake failure.
send() in CONNECTING state throws InvalidStateError; check readyState or queue.
wss:// is required on HTTPS pages (mixed content).
Reconnect with exponential backoff, jitter and a heartbeat.

Production-style WebSocket client

interview.q: Why does the WebSocket onerror event have no message?
interview.a: To prevent scripts from probing the network (port scanning) the browser hides details. Use the close code, the Console and the Network tab.

interview.q: What does close code 1006 mean?
interview.a: The connection closed abnormally without a close frame: network failure, server crash, failed handshake or proxy timeout. It is reported locally and never sent over the wire.

interview.q: How should a client handle disconnects?
interview.a: Reconnect with exponential backoff and jitter, queue outgoing messages, re-subscribe after reconnect and use heartbeats to detect dead connections.

pitfalls: Catching an OOM-style RangeError and continuing may leave the app in a bad state; free memory first.
Increasing --max-old-space-size hides a leak, it does not fix it.
topics.title: Memory Leaks vs "Out of Memory" Errors
topics.summary: Which memory errors are catchable (RangeError) and which crash the tab, the usual leak sources and how to find them.
topics.description:
### Two different problems
- A **memory leak**: memory that is no longer needed is still reachable, so the garbage collector cannot free it. Memory grows slowly until the page becomes slow or crashes.
- **Out of memory (OOM)**: you try to allocate more than the engine allows at once or in total.

### What you can catch
| Error | Where | Catchable? |
|---|---|---|
| `RangeError: Invalid string length` | string larger than ~512 MB (V8: 2^29-24 chars) | yes |
| `RangeError: Invalid array length` | length > 2^32 - 1 | yes |
| `RangeError: Array buffer allocation failed` / `Invalid array buffer length` | huge `ArrayBuffer` / typed array | yes |
| `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` | recursion | yes |
| `WebAssembly.Memory(): could not allocate memory` | wasm | yes |
| Chrome "Aw, Snap! Error code: Out of Memory" (STATUS_RESULT_CODE_HUNG / OOM) | tab killed | **no** |
| Node: `FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory` | process killed | **no** |
| `QuotaExceededError` | storage | yes |

Node's default old-space limit depends on RAM (about 2-4 GB). Increase with `node --max-old-space-size=4096 app.js` only after checking for leaks.

### Common leak sources
1. **Event listeners** never removed (`addEventListener` in a component without cleanup). Use `{ signal }` or `removeEventListener`.
2. **Timers / intervals** never cleared (`setInterval` keeps closures alive).
3. **Closures** capturing large objects (a callback keeps a big array reachable).
4. **Global variables** and caches (`Map` that only grows). Use `WeakMap`/`WeakRef`/LRU limits.
5. **Detached DOM nodes** referenced from JS after removal.
6. **Unbounded arrays** (logs, history, undo stacks, message queues).
7. **Subscriptions / observers** not unsubscribed (RxJS, WebSocket, ResizeObserver, MutationObserver).
8. **Promises that never settle** hold their closures.

### Finding leaks
Chrome DevTools → **Memory**: take heap snapshots, perform the action, snapshot again, compare ("Objects allocated between snapshots", filter *Detached*); **Performance monitor** (JS heap size, DOM nodes, listeners); Node: `--inspect`, `process.memoryUsage()`, `heapdump`.

A saw-tooth heap graph (grow, GC drop) is healthy; a rising staircase is a leak.
keyPoints: RangeError allocation messages are catchable; browser tab or Node heap OOM is a crash.
Leaks come from listeners, timers, closures, global caches and detached DOM nodes.
Always clean up in teardown: removeEventListener, clearInterval, unsubscribe, AbortController.
Use WeakMap/WeakRef or size-limited caches for derived data.
Compare heap snapshots in DevTools to find retained objects.

examples.title: Catchable allocation errors
Leaky vs clean: listeners and timers
Bounded cache instead of a growing Map
examples.explanation: The cache never grows beyond its limit, so it cannot leak unboundedly.

interview.q: What is the difference between a memory leak and an out-of-memory error?
interview.a: A leak is unreachable-in-practice but still referenced memory that grows over time. OOM is the failure when allocations exceed the limit; a leak is a common cause of eventual OOM.

interview.q: What are the most common JavaScript leak sources?
interview.a: Forgotten event listeners and timers, closures holding large data, unbounded global caches or arrays, detached DOM nodes still referenced, and unsubscribed observers.

interview.q: How do you find a leak in Chrome?
interview.a: Use the Memory panel: take a heap snapshot, repeat the suspect action, take another and compare retained objects (filter Detached DOM nodes), or record an allocation timeline.
